newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mongolia aims to raise gold output by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia aims to raise gold output by 2000.

text.p: Mongolia plans to boost gold output to around 10 tonnes by the end of the century from 6.1 tonnes it produced last year, the chief of Mongolia's Mining division said on Thursday.

"The top priority in Mongolian industry is mining and the government regards mineral resources as the way to economic revovery," Tsendiin Enkhbold, the mining chief in the country's Agriculture and Industry ministry said.
He said in a paper presented at a mining conference companies like RTZ-CRA and Broken Hill Proprietary are among those who have received the 170 exploration licences issued to date.

"Mongolian companies involved in gold placer developments are looking for Western partners to obtain modern equipment and technology for alluvial mining and gold recover," the Mongolian official added.
Mongolia, which shook off control by the defunct Soviet Union a few years ago, also wants to develop promising areas that may contain silver, copper, tin, tungsten, molybdenum and coal.
A new minerals law was approved on May 1 to facilitate exploration in the country.
